Study_Title: Pre-trained Model-based Automated Software Vulnerability Repair: How Far are We?
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
M1_Evidence_Notes: Standalone fine-tuned pre-trained models; custom C abstraction tool only; no compiler/SAST/feedback loop (Sec. 3-4).
M2_Evidence_Notes: Exact match (Accuracy@K) only; no compilation or test execution because datasets lack tests; manual check of ChatGPT outputs (Sec. 3.3, 5.3, 7).
M3_Evidence_Notes: 8,482 real CVE fixes (Big-Vul + CVEfixes), five pre-trained models, VRepair baseline, ablations of pre-processing/training/inference (Sec. 4).
M4_Evidence_Notes: Replication package (data, scripts, models) released; no deployment or practitioner evaluation (Introduction).
Evidence_Basis: Mean of two authors scoring the full text independently (sheet Validation_29)

Study_Title: VulRepair: A T5-Based Automated Software Vulnerability Repair

M3_Evidence_Notes: 8,482 real fixes from 1,754 projects; baselines VRepair and CodeBERT; ablations on pre-training, tokenizer, architecture (Sec. 4-6).
M4_Evidence_Notes: Code and data released on GitHub/Zenodo; no deployment study (Data Availability).
Evidence_Basis: Mean of two authors scoring the full text independently (sheet Validation_29)

Study_Title: Mystique: Automated Vulnerability Patch Porting with Semantic and Syntactic-Enhanced LLM
M1_Evidence_Notes: Joern slicing, tree-sitter syntax completion, Clang-tidy checks and anomaly-driven refinement loop around a LoRA fine-tuned LLM (Sec. 3).
M2_Evidence_Notes: Exact match / semantic equivalence to developer-ported patches with manual review; no test or PoC execution (Sec. 4.1, 4.8).
M3_Evidence_Notes: 694 CVEs / 1,359 functions, C and Java, strong baselines (TSBPORT, FixMorph, PPatHF, GPT-4o), release-date split against leakage (Sec. 4).
M4_Evidence_Notes: 34 pull requests submitted for 16 CVEs, 29 merged upstream; code and data on Zenodo (Sec. 4.7, 7).
Evidence_Basis: Mean of two authors scoring the full text independently (sheet Validation_29)

Study_Title: Vul-R2: A Reasoning LLM for Automated Vulnerability Repair
M1_Evidence_Notes: LLM critic and rule-based rewards during RL training; no compiler, sandbox or analyser in the loop (Sec. II-C).
M2_Evidence_Notes: Exact match and CodeBLEU only; no compilation, tests or PoC (Sec. III-D).
M3_Evidence_Notes: PrimeVul (435 test) + SVEN (384), seven baselines incl. VulMaster and o3, ablations (Sec. III).
M4_Evidence_Notes: Code and training data released on GitHub; no deployment (Sec. VII).

Study_Title: LLM4CVE: Enabling Iterative Automated Vulnerability Repair with Large Language Models
M1_Evidence_Notes: Iterative self-refinement driven by CodeBLEU change, capped at two iterations; no compiler/SAST in the loop (Sec. 4.5, 5.6).
M2_Evidence_Notes: CodeBLEU plus human ratings, compilation on a subset and one dynamic harness case; no systematic tests or PoC (Sec. 5.8, 6.2-6.3).
M3_Evidence_Notes: 1,856 real CVE function pairs across 8 CWEs and four LLMs, but only internal ablations as baselines (Sec. 5).
M4_Evidence_Notes: Release of apparatus and weights stated on project website (not verified); effort comparison reported (Sec. 6.4, 9).
Evidence_Basis: Mean of two authors scoring the full text independently (sheet Validation_29)
